method: Read-only causal and forensic inspection of experimental telemetry, code, and schemas

arm_b.semantics: PLAN-CONSISTENT DIAGNOSTIC (critical-first, planned charge prioritized, residual to non-critical)

causal_interpretation.core_finding: Arm B does NOT merely correct an isolated battery-charge mismatch; it imposes an unapproved operational policy that brown-outs non-critical loads to prioritize battery charging.
causal_interpretation.priority_hierarchy_arm_a: Total Load (Critical + Non-Critical) > Battery Charging > Curtailment
causal_interpretation.priority_hierarchy_arm_b: Critical Load > Battery Charging > Flexible Load > Non-Critical Load > Curtailment
causal_interpretation.planning_model_structural_cause: The MILP objective prices critical unmet load (J1) and reserve shortfall (J2), but leaves non-critical load unpriced (0 penalty). Non-critical load is shed by construction (Layer B p_served + unmet_crit = p_crit). The planned charge exists because the planning model ignored non-critical load.

why_control_changes_substantially.mechanism: Control B has large unconditional 6-hour lookahead EBR targets, planning mean 36.7 kW battery charge at hour 0. Arm B forces this charge into the battery, shedding 6.1 kW of customer load at hour 0 and 2,557 kWh across the campaign.

why_candidate_sw_changes_fail_to_pass.mechanism: Candidate SW did NOT improve load service under Arm B (it shed 1,533 kWh more load). It passed Gate 2 solely because Control B degraded by 5.19 pp, while Candidate SW degraded by only 3.29 pp due to having lower planned charging at hour 0 from wind crediting.

third_formulation_feasibility.reason: Choosing between serving non-critical customer loads and charging battery reserves during energy deficit is fundamentally a Microgrid Operating Policy decision, not an algorithmic bug fix. An executor cannot resolve an economic trade-off that the planning model refused to price.

governance_verdict.policy_blocker_summary: Promoting SW based on Arm B would deploy an algorithm whose apparent safety depends on degrading microgrid customer service by 1,532 kWh. Promoting S based on Arm A deploys an algorithm whose evaluation deviates from its own planned charging. Formal governance policy determination is required.

required_next_steps.option_1_customer_first: Formally mandate that customer service strictly precedes battery charging (Arm A). Candidate S is confirmed winner (23.11%), SW is permanently disqualified.
required_next_steps.option_2_coordinated_demand_response: Formally authorize planned non-critical load shedding, but PRICE non-critical load in the MILP objective (value of lost load V_LL). Require a new preregistered campaign.
